legend: Bone marrow aspirate smear shows small to intermediate-sized blasts with high N:C ratios, pale basophilic cytoplasm with multiple cytoplasmic blebs or pseudopodal projections, fine chromatin, and small nucleoli (Giemsa) (<<29239>>). A typical binucleated large blast with a high N:C ratio (Giemsa) (<<30127>>).
Bone marrow aspirate smear. Blasts are small to intermediate in size with pseudopods / cytoplasmic blebs. Here, blasts are clustering and mimicking a solid tumour.

Bone marrow biopsy demonstrates sheets of blasts of intermediate size with small amounts of cytoplasm, irregular nuclear contours, occasional binucleation, and dispersed chromatin with distinct nucleoli (<<29998>>). Sheets of intermediate to large blasts with dispersed chromatin and prominent nucleoli are intermixed with immature megakaryocytes and micromegakaryocytes (<<30295>>). Prominent fibrosis with entrapped blasts and immature megakaryocytes (<<30293>>). Higher magnification highlights entrapped blasts and micromegakaryocytes (<<30294>>).

Flow cytometry dot plots show the immunophenotype of blasts (red), monocytes (purple), lymphocytes (light blue), and granulocytes (brown). The blasts show dim CD45 and low side scatter (A), moderate to negative CD34 and heterogeneous CD61 (B), moderate to negative CD41 and KIT (CD117) in a subset (C), bright CD33 and heterogeneous HLA-DR (D), heterogeneous CD42b and bright CD36 (E), and dim to negative CD7 and dim CD4 (F) expression.
